verdict.rationale: Algolia's Search API explicitly supports adding, updating, and configuring individual records via API calls (algolia-docs-4, algolia-docs-31), and its data-sync connectors handle scheduled retries/transformations without redeploying code (algolia-docs-48), implying incremental (non-full-reindex) updates are core to the platform. However, the evidence pack never explicitly states or quantifies 'near real-time' indexing latency after adds/updates/deletes, nor does it discuss delete propagation or any SLA around indexing speed. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of indexing latency/near-real-time guarantees, confirmation that deletes are also near-instant, and any independent/hands-on evidence corroborating update-to-searchable latency.
